It is essential for our long-term development and is critical for the implementation of the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for Small Island Developing States. The countries of our region, as well as other SIDS, face the complex interlinked challenges of climate vulnerability, debt sustainability, narrow production bases, and high exposure to exogenous shocks. South-South cooperation and SIDS to SIDS partnerships in particular are uniquely positioned to leverage shared experiences, facilitate coordination and mutually support implementation in a context of regional solidarity to address shared challenges. Member states of CARICOM are increasingly using South-South and triangular cooperation as an avenue to strengthen the region's resilience. Countries are learning from each other's innovations in renewable energy, disaster risk reduction, and sustainable tourism. In the energy sector, for example, the Caribbean Centre for Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency and the University of the West Indies provide training, knowledge sharing, and capacity building in e-mobility, in regulations and planning workshops, and renewable energy technologies. The CARICOM Hub for the Capacity Building Programme related to multilateral environmental agreements in Africa, Caribbean and Pacific countries project and the CARICOM Technical and Scientific Cooperation Centre provides structured capacity building, technical assistance, training and knowledge sharing support to CARICOM member states and institutions to strengthen skills in environmental management priority areas such as biodiversity conservation, negotiations, chemicals and waste management standards, and scientific cooperation. Collaboration among member states ensures that expertise is developed and retained nationally and regionally, and applied within the Caribbean context. Coordinated emergency response mechanisms, shared resources and logistics strengthen the region's resilience against hurricanes and climate shocks. The Caribbean Disaster Emergency Management Agency exemplifies a best practice model of South-South cooperation that is directly relevant to the implementation of the ABAS. Through established mechanisms for South-South cooperation, CARICOM's relations with traditional and emerging donors, as well as regional blocks of the Global South, continue to deepen collaboration in critical areas. including trade, medicine and healthcare, capacity building, agriculture and food security, sports, renewable energy and climate change, innovation, technology, culture, the ocean economy and maritime security. Countries of the Global South are not merely recipients of development assistance. Through South-South and triangular cooperation, they continue to lead the charge to find transformative solutions for overlapping crises. Today's launch of the Global Alliance for South-South and Triangular Cooperation represents a significant step in facilitating partnerships and strengthening collective action for sustainable development. The future of South-South and triangular cooperation is one of mainstreamed, dynamic and high-impact collaboration, driven by bold ambition and sustained commitment. Let this United Nations Day for South-South Cooperation serve as a moment for the collective renewal of our commitment to solidarity, inclusivity, and innovative development in the Global South. CARICOM stands ready to engage with all partners in shaping a sustainable future that leaves no one behind. I thank you. I.
